drivingQuestion: Why is the sota's offering animal food?
outcomeNote: R' Meir's reason rejected; RG's allegory stands.

segments.he: דְּשַׁמְעֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּקָאָמַר: הִיא הֶאֱכִילַתּוּ מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם — לְפִיכָךְ קׇרְבָּנָהּ מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה. אָמַר לוֹ: הָתִינַח עֲשִׁירָה, עֲנִיָּה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר! אֶלָּא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּעֲשֶׂיהָ מַעֲשֵׂה בְהֵמָה — כָּךְ קׇרְבָּנָהּ מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה.
segments.en: And why did Rabban Gamliel speak up? It was «because he heard Rabbi Meir saying» an alternative explanation: «She fed him,» i.e., her paramour, «delicacies from around the world; therefore, her offering is animal food.» Rabban Gamliel «said to him:» Your explanation «works out well» in the case of «a rich» sota, but with regard to «a poor» sota, who cannot afford such delicacies, «what is there to say? Rather,» the reason she brings an offering of animal food is: «Just as her actions were the actions of an animal, so too her offering is animal food.»
